name: vasculitis overview
title: Vasculitis: suspect it in a chronically unwell patient with several organs involved and no infection or cancer; a new headache over 50 points to giant cell arteritis, sinus, lung, kidney and nerve disease to ANCA-associated vasculitis, purpura on the legs to cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis, and an identifiable cause to secondary vasculitis; each column gives presentation, numbered investigations and treatment in order

root.title: Suspect PRIMARY vasculitis: chronically unwell + several organs + NO infection or cancer found
lines: when: chronically unwell (fevers, chills, weight loss) · several organ systems · purpura · very sick, multi-organ failure · lung hemorrhage + renal dysfunction

every patient: head-to-toe history and exam · blood count, creatinine, liver enzymes, sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP), urinalysis · chest X-ray · cancer screening up to date · URGENT rheumatology
inflammation (non-specific): normocytic anemia (Hb ↓, MCV normal) · reactive thrombocytosis · ESR, CRP ↑ · albumin ↓ (chronic)
kidneys and lungs can be SILENT: creatinine, blood + protein in urine, chest X-ray · rule out INFECTION before immunosuppressing

head: h
Giant cell arteritis (GCA)
large vessel · the most common vasculitis
only over 50 (most over 70)
lifetime risk 1% women, 0.5% men · Northern European
pres: • scalp tender: hurts to brush the hair
• untreated: both eyes, days to months
• limb claudication · Raynaud's · chest pain · arthritis
inv: case: Hb 99 · ESR 70 · CRP 50 · WBC, platelets normal
• or Doppler 'halo sign' (wall edema): specificity > 85%, absent in ~30%, specialty centres only
tx: after blood is drawn · NEVER wait for results

head: h
ANCA-associated vasculitis
anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody · small vessel
granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA)
microscopic (MPA) · eosinophilic (EGPA)
rare · FATAL untreated · relapses common
pres: • bloody crusty nose, sinus pain · saddle nose (GPA)
• dyspnea: nodules, severe adult-onset asthma, PE
inv: 2 · ANCA ONLY if small vessel suspected
• else: orbit, sinus, lung nodule, node, kidney, sural nerve
tx: Unstable, lung bleed, renal failure → ADMIT

head: h
Cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis
small vessel · alone or part of another type
inv: • purpura: punch biopsy in primary care
• ulcer: deep excision by a surgeon
tx: only if severe, other agents failed, infection excluded
30 mg for 1 week, then ↓ 5 mg every 5 days

head: h
Secondary vasculitis
an identifiable underlying cause
pres: • viral: hepatitis B or C, HIV, COVID-19

panels.title: Classify by vessel size
items: small: ANCA trio, cryoglobulinemia, cutaneous leukocytoclastic, Henoch-Schönlein

panels.title: Giant cell arteritis: differential
items: migraine, cluster · meningitis, encephalitis · neck pain
